tags: why does my dog spin at the door
script: The leash comes off the hook and your dog turns into a spinning, whining tornado at the door, and that's not chaos for no reason, it's pure anticipation. Your dog has learned exactly what that sequence of sounds and movements means, the leash, your shoes, the jingle of keys, and their brain releases a burst of dopamine the moment they recognize the pattern, the same anticipation chemical involved in any reward your brain expects but hasn't received yet. Spinning specifically happens because that excess energy has nowhere else to go in a small space, so it comes out as tight, repetitive movement instead of a full sprint. It's the same underlying mechanism as the treat-bag reaction, learned associations plus a flood of anticipatory dopamine equals big, uncontainable excitement. A quick training fix many trainers use is waiting for calm before opening the door, which slowly teaches the brain that calm, not chaos, is what actually gets rewarded.
